svg.title: Peru ENSO Observatory architecture: full diagram
svg.desc: Official ENSO sources, hazard alerts and news feeds are fetched every night by three collectors: a machine in Peru (21:00), n8n in the cloud (22:50) and GitHub Actions (23:37), following a registry measured every Monday. When a source does not answer, the Peru and n8n copies, the Internet Archive or the previous publication are used. The Python pipeline reads, validates, places news by location and publishes everything at once; the site shows each value with links to the live source and the archived copy. Two watchdogs check the site every 6 hours and incidents become issues.
svg.text: Peru ENSO Observatory architecture: full diagram

Each box says what it is and what it does. Each line carries a number: below, under Connections, is what travels along it, when and why. Boxes with the same border color are of the same kind (sources, collectors, copies, pipeline, publication, site, operations and people). Tags
A1 to A10 open each part's annex: its steps, technologies and fallbacks.
Lines:
data

1 · Sources
2 · Collectors
3 · Copies and fallbacks
4 · Daily pipeline
5 · Publication and site
6 · Operations, monitoring and people

g.title: 1. ENFEN and IGP: Peru's official sources → Peru collector: ENFEN portal and ICEN https. Every night the machine in Peru fetches the ENFEN portal's API and listing, the communiqué PDFs and the ICEN over https, none of which answer from the US. That way the official communiqué arrives even though the portal does not answer cloud servers.

2. ENFEN and IGP: Peru's official sources → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher): DHN mirror and ICEN, direct. Actions requests the ICEN over http and the DHN mirror, which answer from the US. For the portal API and listing it uses the Peru copy first; with none, it tries once.

3. ENFEN and IGP: Peru's official sources → n8n collector (AWS cloud): copy of mirror and ICEN. n8n fetches the ICEN over http and the DHN mirror with its PDFs, leaving a second copy in case Actions gets no valid response.

4. NOAA (CPC and PSL) → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher): 15 products, direct. Each night Actions downloads NOAA's indices, sea temperature, subsurface heat and ENSO discussion. If a critical product fails with no previous value, nothing is deployed.
5. NOAA (CPC and PSL) → n8n collector (AWS cloud): backup copy. n8n fetches 14 of those URLs nightly; if Actions' direct request fails, the pipeline uses that copy. cpc-godas-d20 has no n8n copy.

6. Official hazard alerts (14 sources) → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher): 14 alert sources. Along with the news, Actions reads the INDECI, SENAMHI, DHN, IGP, USGS, PTWC and NASA FIRMS warnings, each in its own format (RSS, JSON, HTML, CSV or text).
7. Official hazard alerts (14 sources) → n8n collector (AWS cloud): backup copy. n8n keeps a copy of the 14 alert sources in case Actions cannot reach them that night.

8. Government pages kept as archive only → Peru collector: archive only, from Peru. The collector downloads these 12 fixed-list pages nightly to keep the original. 6 of them (4 SENAMHI web pages, 2 ANA) do not answer from the US.

9. Government pages kept as archive only → n8n collector (AWS cloud): the 6 on n8n. IMARPE, CENEPRED, the SENAMHI observatory and IDESEP carry the n8n channel by rule (open or unmeasured), so n8n downloads them too. The daily run does not request them since they have no parser.

10. Media and government: 116 news feeds → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher): 116 news feeds. Each night Actions reads the government, national, regional, radio and international feeds, one after another per server as a courtesy. UN News and Sin Rodeos are requested as a feed reader.

11. Media and government: 116 news feeds → n8n collector (AWS cloud): backup copy (114). n8n fetches the same feeds except the 2 reader ones; if one fails from Actions, the pipeline uses the newest copy.

12. Google News: 38 searches → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher): feed reader, once per 20 h. Because their robots.txt forbids these 38 feeds, Actions requests them like an RSS reader: main only, no retry and at most once every 20 h. Between reads the last one is repeated.

13. Each server's robots.txt → Weekly reachability probe: longest rule wins. Each week the probe reads every server's robots.txt before measuring. A forbidden path becomes robots-disallowed and loses its channels, except reader feeds.

14. Each server's robots.txt → Peru collector: obeyed live. Each night the collector reads robots.txt before requesting. It skips forbidden paths, and if robots.txt does not answer it asks nothing of that server.

15. Weekly reachability probe → Registry builder: measures and rebuilds. The probe writes reachability.json with what Actions, Peru and n8n measured, then runs build_registry right away so the channels follow the new measurements.

16. Registry builder → Source registry (registry/): generates and validates. Writes sources.json with status and channels per URL. On main the probe commits registry/; on other branches the result goes to bot/registry/<branch>.

17. data-peru branch → Weekly reachability probe: what Peru measured. The probe reads Peru's index.json: each URL's result there plus extra measurements. So the registry can confirm a geoblock or an outage; there are no Peru measurements yet.

18. data-n8n branch → Weekly reachability probe: what n8n measured. It also adds n8n's last attempt on AWS as a measurement for the n8n network. A carried copy counts as its last failure, not as today's measurement.

19. Source registry (registry/) → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher): per-URL channel plan. Each run the pipeline reads who fetches each URL. What the registry does not give to Actions is read from the copies (with no copy, it is requested directly once), forbidden URLs are not requested and the 40 reader feeds are requested at most every 20 h, only on main.

20. Source registry (registry/) → n8n collector (AWS cloud): 152 URLs for n8n. At start n8n reads the registry from main on GitHub (or the copy built into the flow) and requests only the URLs assigned to n8n.

21. Source registry (registry/) → Peru collector: peru-server URLs and PDFs. The collector reads the registry from GitHub with its token (or the kit copy), adds the peru-server URLs and their PDF-follow rules to its fixed list, and probes up to 60 unknown, suspected-geoblock or down URLs this run did not request.

22. Development tools → Registry builder: verified sources into catalogue. A person reviews the probe reports and adds the working feeds and parsers to the code; from there they enter the registry. That is how the 2026-10-21 catalogue was built.

23. Peru collector → data-peru branch: copies, heartbeat, probes. When done it pushes index.json, the files, heartbeat.json and its measurements to data-peru. If nothing answered, it pushes only the heartbeat and leaves the last good copy untouched.
24. data-peru branch → Peru collector: previous copy. Before pushing, the collector reads its previous copy and keeps for up to 72 h the URLs that failed tonight, flagged carried.

25. Peru collector → Daily update (observatory.yml): asks to refresh (enso-refresh). After pushing it sends repository_dispatch enso-refresh so the site updates without waiting for 23:37. If a run is in progress, it queues. It is on by default in the kit.

26. n8n collector (AWS cloud) → data-n8n branch: commit replaces the branch. n8n uploads new files via the GitHub API, builds a parentless commit and moves data-n8n. index.json and heartbeat.json always go, even if nothing answered.
27. data-n8n branch → n8n collector (AWS cloud): previous copy. Its 'Leer copia anterior' node reads data-n8n's index.json and keeps for up to 72 h the URLs that failed tonight, flagged carried.

28. Collector kit and check → Peru machine operator: kit .zip and VERIFICAR. The person downloads recolector-peru.zip from the recolector-kit release and runs VERIFICAR (the report is saved in logs/ to send in). The machine does not update itself: a new kit is installed with ACTUALIZAR.

29. Peru machine operator → Peru collector: installs, token, task. Running INSTALAR with the token registers the 21:00 scheduled task. The collector shows a desktop notice after 2 failures or if the token expires in under 21 days.
30. Maintainers and owner → Peru machine operator: token and kit. They hand over a fine-grained GitHub token (this repository only) and the kit, and a new one when the collector warns it is expiring.

31. n8n operator (colleague) → n8n collector (AWS cloud): imports and activates. The person imports n8n/dist/enso-n8n-recolector.json into their n8n, picks the GitHub credential and activates it. Nodes are regenerated with build.mjs, not edited in n8n.

32. Maintainers and owner → n8n operator (colleague): GitHub token. They hand over a fine-grained token (this repository only, Contents read and write, 1 year) for the n8n credential. n8n gives no warning before it expires: once it does, the copy stops uploading and relay-n8n-stale appears.

33. Daily update (observatory.yml) → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher): starts the pipeline. The «Fetch, validate and build» step runs python -m enso.observatory with the Peru and n8n copies, the history and the reader state already fetched, with a 26-minute limit.

34. data-peru branch → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher): Peru copy (relay-peru). If Actions gets no valid response, or the URL is Peru-only, it uses the data-peru copy: up to 7 days old, status 200 and a verified sha256.
35. data-n8n branch → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher): n8n copy (relay-n8n). The same with n8n copies, valid up to 72 h. If Peru and n8n both have a copy of the same URL, the newest wins.

36. Internet Archive (Wayback) → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher): archived copy. If the URL, the mirror and the copies fail, the latest Wayback copy is used, with its date. For ENFEN (listing and PDF) a fresh one is requested if there is none or the existing one is over a day old.

37. Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) → Official source reading: response with provenance. Each response arrives with body, channel, URL, copy date, sha256 and attempts; if everything failed, the error arrives with the attempts.

38. Previous publication (live data/) → Official source reading: last valid value. The previous publication's sources/<id>.json is read to compare the format fingerprint. If the source fails, that value is reused with its real date, flagged carried.

39. Official source reading → Series, statuses and GRD signal: data and communiqué. The data of the 17 sources, fresh or carried, and the latest ENFEN communiqué go on to build the series, the weekly data and the official statuses.

40. Reference data: places and thresholds → Series, statuses and GRD signal: GRD thresholds. Each indicator gets its GRD colour from expert-grd-image-v1.yaml. A value between intervals is 'unclassified', never normal. ICEN categories are fixed in signals.py.

41. Series, statuses and GRD signal → Publication write and validation: series, statuses, GRD signal. The series, weekly data, ENFEN and NOAA statuses, ICEN events and the GRD signal go into series.json, weekly.json, the CSVs and dashboard.json.

42. Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) → News and alerts: reading and filtering: feed bodies. Feeds are downloaded with two dedicated clients (normal, and single-try for reader feeds) that share the Peru and n8n copies but never use the Internet Archive.

43. Actions cache: reader feeds → News and alerts: reading and filtering: reader state (read and save). At start it restores when each reader feed was last requested and its unpublished items. Without the cache they are not requested, except on the first publication. Each request is noted before it is made and the state is saved at the end even if the run fails.

44. Previous publication (live data/) → News and alerts: reading and filtering: previous feed status. The previous publication's news/feeds.json is read (3 tries): together with the cache it gives each reader feed's last request time, so none is repeated within 20 h.

45. News and alerts: reading and filtering → Append-only news history: new placed items. Today's relevant items and still-unpublished reader-feed items, with their hazards and place, are appended to the history if their id is new.

46. Previous publication (live data/) → Append-only news history: previous history. news/items.jsonl is read (up to 3 tries on server errors). If it arrives, it is completed from the data-archive copy; if not, it is rebuilt from that copy or, without one, flagged restarted.

47. data-archive branch → Append-only news history: full history copy. Before the pipeline, sources/news/items.jsonl.gz is downloaded via the GitHub API. It is used to add missing items or rebuild the history if the site did not serve it.
48. Append-only news history → Placement and place corrections: the whole history. The whole history, old and new, is re-placed and corrected in one go; the stored JSONL text does not change.

49. Reference data: places and thresholds → Placement and place corrections: UBIGEO and boundaries. INEI names let a place be recognised in the text, and IGN boundaries tell which district, province or department a coordinate falls in.

50. Places console (/admin/) → Placement and place corrections: current corrections. With Cloudflare, the pipeline requests GET /api/geo/overrides (20 s timeout) and applies each item's latest correction. With GitHub Pages there is no console and this step does not happen.

51. Previous publication (live data/) → Placement and place corrections: previous corrections. If the console is absent or does not answer, the previous publication's geo/overrides.json is used; if that cannot be read either, none is applied (they stay stored in D1).

52. Placement and place corrections → Publication write and validation: items, clusters, alerts. The history goes on as stored and, with corrected places, items.csv, the 14-day clusters, the 7-day alerts for feed.json and the geo/ files for the console.

53. Previous publication (live data/) → Publication write and validation: previous copies and news. If a source did not answer, the archived copy the previous publication had is republished. If news reading failed, its news/ and geo/ are reused with carriedFrom.

54. Official source reading → Incident log: failures, carries, format. It logs unreachable (error for critical sources), format-drift, format-changed, carried-forward and communique-unread, outlook-unread (the communiqué outlook could not be read) and informe-* (the technical report was not downloaded, could not be read or part of it failed validation; when no route answers it is only a warning). When the newest communiqué or its report cannot be downloaded by any route, manual-download-needed (warning) lists them for the documents console.

55. Series, statuses and GRD signal → Incident log: stale data and statuses. It logs stale-<series> and stale-weekly (data past its deadline), official-overdue (the expected NOAA or ENFEN bulletin did not arrive), newer-communique-unparsed (a newer communiqué could not be read), status-unknown (error: no ENFEN status), informe-icen-mismatch (the technical report's ICEN differs from IGP's) and late-<item> (the next one was due and has not arrived).

56. data-peru branch → Incident log: Peru copy health. At start the pipeline reads data-peru's index.json and heartbeat.json and logs relay-missing, relay-stale (over 36 h), relay-sources-down, relay-goal-missed or relay-token-expiring. That is how a machine that is off becomes an issue.
57. data-n8n branch → Incident log: n8n copy health. The same with data-n8n: relay-n8n-missing, relay-n8n-stale (over 36 h) or relay-n8n-sources-down. That is how a stopped n8n flow becomes an issue.

58. News and alerts: reading and filtering → Incident log: news and history. The news stage logs feeds-reader-unknown, news-degraded, news-history-missing (error if there is no copy either), news-history-restored and news-history-large. They also become issues.

59. Placement and place corrections → Incident log: failed corrections. It logs overrides-http (the console answered with an error), overrides-down (no answer) and overrides-rejected (a correction has invalid codes).

60. Incident log → Publication write and validation: incidents and health. Incidents, the worst severity and the counts go to run-report.json; health.json marks degraded (on error or critical) and dashboard.json keeps the worst severity.

61. Incident log → Deploy and verification: critical: no deploy. With --fail-on critical, a critical worst severity makes the pipeline step exit 1, the build fails and deploy does not run; the previous site stays live.

62. Publication write and validation → Published files (data/): atomic swap of data/. If validation passes (same publicationId everywhere, sorted series, dashboard with official, series and grd), public/data is replaced in one move by the new folder.

63. Published files (data/) → Deploy and verification: public/ ready to test. With data/ written, the build adapts the site's addresses, runs the Chromium browser tests and uploads the site; if one of those steps fails, nothing is deployed.

64. Deploy and verification → Live site (SITE_URL): publishes, verifies live. Uploads the whole site at once to GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, and verify_live waits up to 10 min until dashboard.json and manifest.json carry the new publicationId.

65. Live site (SITE_URL) → Previous publication (live data/): today's is tomorrow's previous. What the site serves today under data/ is what the next run reads with --previous to carry data over and continue the history.

66. Live site (SITE_URL) → Website (10 views): serves pages and data. The host serves index.html, assets/ and data/. The page first fetches dashboard.json and then each file with the same publicationId.

67. Public → Website (10 views): opens the site or downloads. Anyone opens the page or downloads the CSV and JSON in data/ directly; from each value they can go to the live source or the archived copy.

68. Daily update (observatory.yml) → archive job: after a good build on main. The build leaves the raw-sources artifact (7 days) with the new raw responses and the news history; the archive job downloads it in parallel with deploy.

69. archive job → data-archive branch: append only, never deletes. Adds the responses it lacked, appends the day's items and merges the history with merge_history.py. Rejects commits with deletions and tries the push up to 3 times.

70. Published files (data/) → Incident issues (incidente-datos): run-report to issues. The incidents job downloads run-report.json and opens, updates or closes one issue per fingerprint. If build, deploy or archive fail, it also opens 'La actualización diaria falló'.

71. Incident issues (incidente-datos) → Maintainers and owner: alerts to review. Maintainers see the open incidents labelled incidente-datos; they close by themselves once the problem stops appearing.
72. Live site (SITE_URL) → GitHub watchdog (watchdog.yml): reads dashboard.json. Every 6 hours it fetches data/dashboard.json without cache and computes the publication age from generatedAt.

73. GitHub watchdog (watchdog.yml) → Daily update (observatory.yml): re-runs past 30 h. If the publication is over 30 h old or unreadable, it starts the daily update, unless one is running or one was dispatched, by hand or by it, in the last 6 h.

74. GitHub watchdog (watchdog.yml) → Incident issues (incidente-datos): 'site stale' issue. Opens or comments 'El sitio publicado está desactualizado' with the action taken, and closes it once the site is current again.
75. Live site (SITE_URL) → n8n watchdog (outside GitHub): reads manifest.json. Every 6 hours, from outside GitHub, n8n fetches data/manifest.json and checks that generatedAt is under 30 h old.

76. n8n watchdog (outside GitHub) → n8n operator (colleague): Error workflow, if set. If the colleague set up an n8n Error workflow (for example, an email), a failed execution triggers it. It works even if GitHub switched its scheduled workflows off.

77. Published files (data/) → Places console (/admin/): items to review. The console loads data/geo/items.json (up to 4000 items, 120 days) and ubigeo.json for its pickers; the API also uses ubigeo.json to reject unknown codes.

78. Maintainers and owner → Place reviewers: reviewer accounts. tools.geo_users creates each reviewer's username and password; the owner loads the GEO_USERS secret and binds the D1 database GEO_DB in Cloudflare.

79. Place reviewers → Places console (/admin/): correct places. Logged in, they set, confirm or mark each item as national or 'not in Peru'. Each change is a new row in the D1 database, applied in the next run (23:37 or an earlier one).

80. Maintainers and owner → Daily update (observatory.yml): merge to main or manual. Each push to main publishes right away (unless only .md or docs/ changed). It can also be run by hand, choosing whether to request fresh Internet Archive copies.

81. Maintainers and owner → Development tools: PRs, claude/** branches, manual. ci.yml runs on every PR and claude/** push; n8n.yml when n8n/ changes. Probes and captures: by hand or when their tool changes on claude/**. Their results are pulled by hand from the bot/ branches.

82. Published files (data/) → Documents console (/admin/documentos.html): pending documents. The console shows data/manual-needed.json: each document the run could not download, with links to open it in a browser, the reason and, if an uploaded copy failed, why.

83. Maintainers and owner → Documents console (/admin/documentos.html): download and upload the PDF. Prompted by the manual-download-needed issue, an administrator opens the document in their browser, passes the human check themselves (the system never evades it), saves the PDF and uploads it.

84. Documents console (/admin/documentos.html) → data-manual branch: commit with the PDF. Streams the PDF blob, builds a tree with the new index.json, commits and fast-forwards the branch; if another upload moved it, it retries once.

85. Documents console (/admin/documentos.html) → Daily update (observatory.yml): asks to refresh (enso-refresh). After saving the PDF, the API sends repository_dispatch enso-refresh: the refresh starts right away instead of waiting for 23:37.

86. data-manual branch → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher): uploaded copy (relay-manual). The pipeline finds it by the document's own URL (or manual://enfen-informe/<id> when unknown). It is validated like any other copy: another number or period is not published and the document stays pending with the reason.
ENFEN and IGP: Peru's official sources. ENFEN's official communiqué (portal and its mirror at the Navy's DHN), which carries the coastal El Niño or La Niña alert status, and IGP's monthly ICEN.

g.title: Official hazard alerts (14 sources). Warnings from INDECI's COEN, SENAMHI (Telegram and 4 GEOSINPAD layers), NASA FIRMS hotspots, USGS earthquakes, DHN bulletins, PTWC messages and IGP volcano alerts (CENVUL).

a.title: Annex A6: News and alerts: reading, filtering, history and place

svg.text: Connections: what travels along each line, when and why
ENFEN portal and ICEN https
ENFEN and IGP: Peru's official sources → Peru collector · daily 21:00 Lima, retries until 23:30
Every night the machine in Peru fetches the ENFEN portal's API and listing, the communiqué
PDFs and the ICEN over https, none of which answer from the US. That way the official
communiqué arrives even though the portal does not answer cloud servers.
DHN mirror and ICEN, direct
ENFEN and IGP: Peru's official sources → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) · daily 23:37
Lima, first in line
Actions requests the ICEN over http and the DHN mirror, which answer from the US. For the
portal API and listing it uses the Peru copy first; with none, it tries once.
copy of mirror and ICEN
ENFEN and IGP: Peru's official sources → n8n collector (AWS cloud) · daily 22:50 Lima
n8n fetches the ICEN over http and the DHN mirror with its PDFs, leaving a second copy in
case Actions gets no valid response.
15 products, direct
NOAA (CPC and PSL) → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) · daily 23:37 Lima
Each night Actions downloads NOAA's indices, sea temperature, subsurface heat and ENSO
discussion. If a critical product fails with no previous value, nothing is deployed.
backup copy
NOAA (CPC and PSL) → n8n collector (AWS cloud) · daily 22:50 Lima
n8n fetches 14 of those URLs nightly; if Actions' direct request fails, the pipeline uses that
copy. cpc-godas-d20 has no n8n copy.
14 alert sources
Official hazard alerts (14 sources) → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) · daily 23:37 Lima
Along with the news, Actions reads the INDECI, SENAMHI, DHN, IGP, USGS, PTWC and NASA
FIRMS warnings, each in its own format (RSS, JSON, HTML, CSV or text).
backup copy
Official hazard alerts (14 sources) → n8n collector (AWS cloud) · daily 22:50 Lima
n8n keeps a copy of the 14 alert sources in case Actions cannot reach them that night.
archive only, from Peru
Government pages kept as archive only → Peru collector · daily 21:00 Lima
The collector downloads these 12 fixed-list pages nightly to keep the original. 6 of them (4
SENAMHI web pages, 2 ANA) do not answer from the US.
the 6 on n8n
Government pages kept as archive only → n8n collector (AWS cloud) · daily 22:50 Lima
IMARPE, CENEPRED, the SENAMHI observatory and IDESEP carry the n8n channel by rule
(open or unmeasured), so n8n downloads them too. The daily run does not request them
since they have no parser.
116 news feeds
Media and government: 116 news feeds → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) · daily 23:37
Lima, after the official sources
Each night Actions reads the government, national, regional, radio and international feeds,
one after another per server as a courtesy. UN News and Sin Rodeos are requested as a
feed reader.
backup copy (114)
Media and government: 116 news feeds → n8n collector (AWS cloud) · daily 22:50 Lima
n8n fetches the same feeds except the 2 reader ones; if one fails from Actions, the pipeline
uses the newest copy.
feed reader, once per 20 h
Google News: 38 searches → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) · at most every 20 h; main
runs only
Because their robots.txt forbids these 38 feeds, Actions requests them like an RSS reader:
main only, no retry and at most once every 20 h. Between reads the last one is repeated.
longest rule wins
Each server's robots.txt → Weekly reachability probe · Mondays 04:17 Lima
Each week the probe reads every server's robots.txt before measuring. A forbidden path
becomes robots-disallowed and loses its channels, except reader feeds.
obeyed live
Each server's robots.txt → Peru collector · daily 21:00 Lima
Each night the collector reads robots.txt before requesting. It skips forbidden paths, and if
robots.txt does not answer it asks nothing of that server.
measures and rebuilds
Weekly reachability probe → Registry builder · Mondays 04:17 Lima (09:17 UTC)
The probe writes reachability.json with what Actions, Peru and n8n measured, then runs
build_registry right away so the channels follow the new measurements.
generates and validates
Registry builder → Source registry (registry/) · Mondays 04:17 Lima
Writes sources.json with status and channels per URL. On main the probe commits registry/;
on other branches the result goes to bot/registry/<branch>.
what Peru measured
data-peru branch → Weekly reachability probe · Mondays 04:17 Lima
The probe reads Peru's index.json: each URL's result there plus extra measurements. So the
registry can confirm a geoblock or an outage; there are no Peru measurements yet.
what n8n measured
data-n8n branch → Weekly reachability probe · Mondays 04:17 Lima
It also adds n8n's last attempt on AWS as a measurement for the n8n network. A carried
copy counts as its last failure, not as today's measurement.
per-URL channel plan
Source registry (registry/) → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) · every observatory.yml run
Each run the pipeline reads who fetches each URL. What the registry does not give to
Actions is read from the copies (with no copy, it is requested directly once), forbidden URLs
are not requested and the 40 reader feeds are requested at most every 20 h, only on main.
152 URLs for n8n
Source registry (registry/) → n8n collector (AWS cloud) · daily 22:50 Lima
At start n8n reads the registry from main on GitHub (or the copy built into the flow) and
requests only the URLs assigned to n8n.
peru-server URLs and PDFs
Source registry (registry/) → Peru collector · daily 21:00 Lima
The collector reads the registry from GitHub with its token (or the kit copy), adds the
peru-server URLs and their PDF-follow rules to its fixed list, and probes up to 60 unknown,
suspected-geoblock or down URLs this run did not request.
verified sources into catalogue
Development tools → Registry builder · by hand
A person reviews the probe reports and adds the working feeds and parsers to the code;
from there they enter the registry. That is how the 2026-10-21 catalogue was built.
copies, heartbeat, probes
Peru collector → data-peru branch · 21:00 to 23:30 Lima
When done it pushes index.json, the files, heartbeat.json and its measurements to
data-peru. If nothing answered, it pushes only the heartbeat and leaves the last good copy
untouched.
previous copy
data-peru branch → Peru collector · daily 21:00 Lima
Before pushing, the collector reads its previous copy and keeps for up to 72 h the URLs that
failed tonight, flagged carried.
asks to refresh (enso-refresh)
Peru collector → Daily update (observatory.yml) · after pushing a copy (not a heartbeat only)
After pushing it sends repository_dispatch enso-refresh so the site updates without waiting
for 23:37. If a run is in progress, it queues. It is on by default in the kit.
commit replaces the branch
n8n collector (AWS cloud) → data-n8n branch · daily 22:50 Lima
n8n uploads new files via the GitHub API, builds a parentless commit and moves data-n8n.
index.json and heartbeat.json always go, even if nothing answered.
previous copy
data-n8n branch → n8n collector (AWS cloud) · daily 22:50 Lima
Its 'Leer copia anterior' node reads data-n8n's index.json and keeps for up to 72 h the URLs
that failed tonight, flagged carried.
kit .zip and VERIFICAR
Collector kit and check → Peru machine operator · when changes to the kit, python/enso/ or the
registry are merged to main (the bot's weekly commit does not count)
The person downloads recolector-peru.zip from the recolector-kit release and runs
VERIFICAR (the report is saved in logs/ to send in). The machine does not update itself: a
new kit is installed with ACTUALIZAR.
installs, token, task
Peru machine operator → Peru collector
Running INSTALAR with the token registers the 21:00 scheduled task. The collector shows a
desktop notice after 2 failures or if the token expires in under 21 days.
token and kit
Maintainers and owner → Peru machine operator
They hand over a fine-grained GitHub token (this repository only) and the kit, and a new
one when the collector warns it is expiring.
imports and activates
n8n operator (colleague) → n8n collector (AWS cloud)
The person imports n8n/dist/enso-n8n-recolector.json into their n8n, picks the GitHub
credential and activates it. Nodes are regenerated with build.mjs, not edited in n8n.
GitHub token
Maintainers and owner → n8n operator (colleague)
They hand over a fine-grained token (this repository only, Contents read and write, 1 year)
for the n8n credential. n8n gives no warning before it expires: once it does, the copy stops
uploading and relay-n8n-stale appears.
starts the pipeline
Daily update (observatory.yml) → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) · 23:37 Lima (04:37
UTC); merge to main; by hand; enso-refresh; watchdog
The «Fetch, validate and build» step runs python -m enso.observatory with the Peru and
n8n copies, the history and the reader state already fetched, with a 26-minute limit.
Peru copy (relay-peru)
data-peru branch → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) · every observatory.yml run
If Actions gets no valid response, or the URL is Peru-only, it uses the data-peru copy: up to 7
days old, status 200 and a verified sha256.
n8n copy (relay-n8n)
data-n8n branch → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) · every observatory.yml run
The same with n8n copies, valid up to 72 h. If Peru and n8n both have a copy of the same
URL, the newest wins.
archived copy
Internet Archive (Wayback) → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) · only if everything before
failed, within the 8 official minutes
If the URL, the mirror and the copies fail, the latest Wayback copy is used, with its date. For
ENFEN (listing and PDF) a fresh one is requested if there is none or the existing one is over
a day old.
response with provenance
Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) → Official source reading
Each response arrives with body, channel, URL, copy date, sha256 and attempts; if
everything failed, the error arrives with the attempts.
last valid value
Previous publication (live data/) → Official source reading · every run
The previous publication's sources/<id>.json is read to compare the format fingerprint. If
the source fails, that value is reused with its real date, flagged carried.
data and communiqué
Official source reading → Series, statuses and GRD signal
The data of the 17 sources, fresh or carried, and the latest ENFEN communiqué go on to
build the series, the weekly data and the official statuses.
GRD thresholds
Reference data: places and thresholds → Series, statuses and GRD signal
Each indicator gets its GRD colour from expert-grd-image-v1.yaml. A value between
intervals is 'unclassified', never normal. ICEN categories are fixed in signals.py.
series, statuses, GRD signal
Series, statuses and GRD signal → Publication write and validation
The series, weekly data, ENFEN and NOAA statuses, ICEN events and the GRD signal go into
series.json, weekly.json, the CSVs and dashboard.json.
feed bodies
Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) → News and alerts: reading and filtering · daily 23:37
Lima, after the official sources
Feeds are downloaded with two dedicated clients (normal, and single-try for reader feeds)
that share the Peru and n8n copies but never use the Internet Archive.
reader state (read and save)
Actions cache: reader feeds → News and alerts: reading and filtering · main runs only
At start it restores when each reader feed was last requested and its unpublished items.
Without the cache they are not requested, except on the first publication. Each request is
noted before it is made and the state is saved at the end even if the run fails.
previous feed status
Previous publication (live data/) → News and alerts: reading and filtering
The previous publication's news/feeds.json is read (3 tries): together with the cache it gives
each reader feed's last request time, so none is repeated within 20 h.
new placed items
News and alerts: reading and filtering → Append-only news history
Today's relevant items and still-unpublished reader-feed items, with their hazards and
place, are appended to the history if their id is new.
previous history
Previous publication (live data/) → Append-only news history
news/items.jsonl is read (up to 3 tries on server errors). If it arrives, it is completed from the
data-archive copy; if not, it is rebuilt from that copy or, without one, flagged restarted.
full history copy
data-archive branch → Append-only news history · at the start of every run
Before the pipeline, sources/news/items.jsonl.gz is downloaded via the GitHub API. It is used
to add missing items or rebuild the history if the site did not serve it.
the whole history
Append-only news history → Placement and place corrections
The whole history, old and new, is re-placed and corrected in one go; the stored JSONL text
does not change.
UBIGEO and boundaries
Reference data: places and thresholds → Placement and place corrections
INEI names let a place be recognised in the text, and IGN boundaries tell which district,
province or department a coordinate falls in.
current corrections
Places console (/admin/) → Placement and place corrections · every run, only with
DEPLOY_TARGET=cloudflare
With Cloudflare, the pipeline requests GET /api/geo/overrides (20 s timeout) and applies
each item's latest correction. With GitHub Pages there is no console and this step does not
happen.
previous corrections
Previous publication (live data/) → Placement and place corrections
If the console is absent or does not answer, the previous publication's geo/overrides.json is
used; if that cannot be read either, none is applied (they stay stored in D1).
items, clusters, alerts
Placement and place corrections → Publication write and validation
The history goes on as stored and, with corrected places, items.csv, the 14-day clusters, the
7-day alerts for feed.json and the geo/ files for the console.
previous copies and news
Previous publication (live data/) → Publication write and validation
If a source did not answer, the archived copy the previous publication had is republished. If
news reading failed, its news/ and geo/ are reused with carriedFrom.
failures, carries, format
Official source reading → Incident log
It logs unreachable (error for critical sources), format-drift, format-changed, carried-forward
and communique-unread, outlook-unread (the communiqué outlook could not be read) and
informe-* (the technical report was not downloaded, could not be read or part of it failed
validation; when no route answers it is only a warning). When the newest communiqué or
its report cannot be downloaded by any route, manual-download-needed (warning) lists
them for the documents console.
stale data and statuses
Series, statuses and GRD signal → Incident log
It logs stale-<series> and stale-weekly (data past its deadline), official-overdue (the
expected NOAA or ENFEN bulletin did not arrive), newer-communique-unparsed (a newer
communiqué could not be read), status-unknown (error: no ENFEN status),
informe-icen-mismatch (the technical report's ICEN differs from IGP's) and late-<item> (the
next one was due and has not arrived).
Peru copy health
data-peru branch → Incident log · every observatory.yml run
At start the pipeline reads data-peru's index.json and heartbeat.json and logs relay-missing,
relay-stale (over 36 h), relay-sources-down, relay-goal-missed or relay-token-expiring. That
is how a machine that is off becomes an issue.
n8n copy health
data-n8n branch → Incident log · every observatory.yml run
The same with data-n8n: relay-n8n-missing, relay-n8n-stale (over 36 h) or
relay-n8n-sources-down. That is how a stopped n8n flow becomes an issue.
news and history
News and alerts: reading and filtering → Incident log
The news stage logs feeds-reader-unknown, news-degraded, news-history-missing (error if
there is no copy either), news-history-restored and news-history-large. They also become
issues.
failed corrections
Placement and place corrections → Incident log
It logs overrides-http (the console answered with an error), overrides-down (no answer) and
overrides-rejected (a correction has invalid codes).
incidents and health
Incident log → Publication write and validation
Incidents, the worst severity and the counts go to run-report.json; health.json marks
degraded (on error or critical) and dashboard.json keeps the worst severity.
critical: no deploy
Incident log → Deploy and verification
With --fail-on critical, a critical worst severity makes the pipeline step exit 1, the build fails
and deploy does not run; the previous site stays live.
atomic swap of data/
Publication write and validation → Published files (data/)
If validation passes (same publicationId everywhere, sorted series, dashboard with official,
series and grd), public/data is replaced in one move by the new folder.
public/ ready to test
Published files (data/) → Deploy and verification
With data/ written, the build adapts the site's addresses, runs the Chromium browser tests
and uploads the site; if one of those steps fails, nothing is deployed.
publishes, verifies live
Deploy and verification → Live site (SITE_URL) · after every successful build
Uploads the whole site at once to GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, and verify_live waits up
to 10 min until dashboard.json and manifest.json carry the new publicationId.
today's is tomorrow's previous
Live site (SITE_URL) → Previous publication (live data/) · in the next run
What the site serves today under data/ is what the next run reads with --previous to carry
data over and continue the history.
serves pages and data
Live site (SITE_URL) → Website (10 views)
The host serves index.html, assets/ and data/. The page first fetches dashboard.json and
then each file with the same publicationId.
opens the site or downloads
Public → Website (10 views)
Anyone opens the page or downloads the CSV and JSON in data/ directly; from each value
they can go to the live source or the archived copy.
after a good build on main
Daily update (observatory.yml) → archive job · every main run whose build passes
The build leaves the raw-sources artifact (7 days) with the new raw responses and the news
history; the archive job downloads it in parallel with deploy.
append only, never deletes
archive job → data-archive branch · after every successful build on main
Adds the responses it lacked, appends the day's items and merges the history with
merge_history.py. Rejects commits with deletions and tries the push up to 3 times.
run-report to issues
Published files (data/) → Incident issues (incidente-datos) · at the end of every run, even a failed
one
The incidents job downloads run-report.json and opens, updates or closes one issue per
fingerprint. If build, deploy or archive fail, it also opens 'La actualización diaria falló'.
alerts to review
Incident issues (incidente-datos) → Maintainers and owner
Maintainers see the open incidents labelled incidente-datos; they close by themselves once
the problem stops appearing.
reads dashboard.json
Live site (SITE_URL) → GitHub watchdog (watchdog.yml) · 19:17, 01:17, 07:17 and 13:17 Lima
Every 6 hours it fetches data/dashboard.json without cache and computes the publication
age from generatedAt.
re-runs past 30 h
GitHub watchdog (watchdog.yml) → Daily update (observatory.yml) · only if the site is behind
If the publication is over 30 h old or unreadable, it starts the daily update, unless one is
running or one was dispatched, by hand or by it, in the last 6 h.
'site stale' issue
GitHub watchdog (watchdog.yml) → Incident issues (incidente-datos) · if stale or recovered
Opens or comments 'El sitio publicado está desactualizado' with the action taken, and
closes it once the site is current again.
reads manifest.json
Live site (SITE_URL) → n8n watchdog (outside GitHub) · every 6 h (n8n interval)
Every 6 hours, from outside GitHub, n8n fetches data/manifest.json and checks that
generatedAt is under 30 h old.
Error workflow, if set
n8n watchdog (outside GitHub) → n8n operator (colleague)
If the colleague set up an n8n Error workflow (for example, an email), a failed execution
triggers it. It works even if GitHub switched its scheduled workflows off.
items to review
Published files (data/) → Places console (/admin/) · when the console opens
The console loads data/geo/items.json (up to 4000 items, 120 days) and ubigeo.json for its
pickers; the API also uses ubigeo.json to reject unknown codes.
reviewer accounts
Maintainers and owner → Place reviewers
tools.geo_users creates each reviewer's username and password; the owner loads the
GEO_USERS secret and binds the D1 database GEO_DB in Cloudflare.
correct places
Place reviewers → Places console (/admin/)
Logged in, they set, confirm or mark each item as national or 'not in Peru'. Each change is a
new row in the D1 database, applied in the next run (23:37 or an earlier one).
merge to main or manual
Maintainers and owner → Daily update (observatory.yml) · on merge or by hand
Each push to main publishes right away (unless only .md or docs/ changed). It can also be
run by hand, choosing whether to request fresh Internet Archive copies.
PRs, claude/** branches, manual
Maintainers and owner → Development tools
ci.yml runs on every PR and claude/** push; n8n.yml when n8n/ changes. Probes and
captures: by hand or when their tool changes on claude/**. Their results are pulled by hand
from the bot/ branches.
pending documents
Published files (data/) → Documents console (/admin/documentos.html) · when the console
opens
The console shows data/manual-needed.json: each document the run could not download,
with links to open it in a browser, the reason and, if an uploaded copy failed, why.
download and upload the PDF
Maintainers and owner → Documents console (/admin/documentos.html)
Prompted by the manual-download-needed issue, an administrator opens the document in
their browser, passes the human check themselves (the system never evades it), saves the
PDF and uploads it.
commit with the PDF
Documents console (/admin/documentos.html) → data-manual branch · on each upload
Streams the PDF blob, builds a tree with the new index.json, commits and fast-forwards the
branch; if another upload moved it, it retries once.
asks to refresh (enso-refresh)
Documents console (/admin/documentos.html) → Daily update (observatory.yml) · on each
upload
After saving the PDF, the API sends repository_dispatch enso-refresh: the refresh starts right
away instead of waiting for 23:37.
uploaded copy (relay-manual)
data-manual branch → Download in GitHub Actions (Fetcher) · every observatory.yml run
The pipeline finds it by the document's own URL (or manual://enfen-informe/<id> when
unknown). It is validated like any other copy: another number or period is not published and
the document stays pending with the reason.
